You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 17 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17 and in the 20-week extension period
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to ask you some questions about your child (or children).

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children **under 16** generally qualify automatically (subject to some conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** typically don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age. If you have multiple children, we can check each one separately.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), eligibility depends on whether Alex is in approved education or training. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to know about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in education or training, or has Alex recently left education?**

Please tell me which applies:
1. **Currently in education or training** - Alex is enrolled in an approved education program or training course
2. **Recently left education** - Alex has left education within the last few months (we'll check if within the extension period)
3. **Neither** - Alex is not in education/training and it's been a while since leaving

Which situation describes Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently left education. He finished school and has signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Alex recently left education and has signed up with the careers service.

Let me check the extension eligibility rules, as there may be a period after leaving education during which you can still claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is relevant to your situation. There's a special 20-week extension period available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education.

**To qualify for this extension, Alex must have:**
1. Left approved education or training within the **last 20 weeks**, AND
2. Registered with a qualifying service (such as a government careers service, Connexions, or armed services)

You mentioned Alex has signed up with the local careers service, which is good!

**Can you tell me:**
1. **When exactly did Alex leave education?** (I need to check if it's within the 20-week window)
2. **Has Alex formally registered with the careers service?** (not just visited, but actually registered)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex left school a couple of months ago and has registered with the careers service - not just visited, but properly signed up with them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's really helpful information. 

So Alex:
- Left school a couple of months ago (which is well within the 20-week window)
- Has properly registered with the careers service (not just visited)

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension period. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children aged 16 or over who work 24 hours or more per week (and are not in approved education/training) don't qualify for Child Benefit.

Please let me know:
- Is Alex currently working?
- If yes, how many hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Since Alex isn't working at all, that's fine for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question about Alex's benefit status:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to know if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in their own name (not as part of your household claim, but in Alex's own right).

Is Alex receiving any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect. Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name, so that's fine.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

This matters because certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility, and the rules vary by region:
- **England**: All apprenticeships disqualify from Child Benefit
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (you CAN claim), but other apprenticeships disqualify

Is Alex:
1. **Not in an apprenticeship at all**, or
2. **In an apprenticeship** (if yes, please tell me what type and which country - England, Scotland, or Wales)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started an apprenticeship. He's just registered with the careers service while he figures out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's absolutely fine.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as the claimant (the person applying for Child Benefit).

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Most people qualify simply by normally living in the UK. However, if your situation is different, there are other ways to qualify, such as:
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Being a Crown servant living abroad
- Living in certain qualifying countries

So, do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so that satisfies the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You can be considered responsible if ANY of these apply:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards their care, including things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents, OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Do any of these apply to you? Most commonly, parents live with their child, but please let me know your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree on who should claim (and the current claimant would need to stop their claim).

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming for Alex, so there's no issue there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Which of these best describes Alex's current living situation?**

1. **In hospital** - Alex is currently staying in hospital
2. **In care** - Alex is in local authority care
3. **Fostered** - Alex is in a foster care arrangement
4. **Living normally at home with you** - None of the above apply

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me - none of those special situations apply.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Just one final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child's accommodation or upkeep. 

Since Alex lives at home with you, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm - is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! The council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!

**Summary:**
You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Specifically:

✅ **Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension** - Since Alex is 17, recently left education (a couple of months ago), and has properly registered with the careers service, he qualifies under the special 20-week extension period for young people aged 16-17 who have left approved education.

✅ **All other criteria met:**
- Alex is not working (under 24 hours/week limit)
- Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- Alex is not in an apprenticeship
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- No one else is claiming for Alex
- The local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation

---

### **Important: The 20-Week Extension Period**

Please note that this extension period is **time-limited**. The extension will end either:
- When the 20 weeks since leaving education expire, OR
- When Alex turns 18, **whichever comes sooner**

So if Alex left school a couple of months ago, you have roughly 3-4 months remaining in this extension period.

---

### **Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply as soon as possible** - You can apply online or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Provide evidence of careers service registration** - Keep documentation showing Alex has registered

**Apply here:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

---

### **Payment Information:**

- Payments are typically made **every 4 weeks**
- If you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits, you may be able to get weekly payments

---

### **High Income Child Benefit Charge:**

⚠️ **Important:** If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge through Self Assessment. You can still claim Child Benefit but may have to pay some or all of it back through tax. You can choose not to receive payments but still register (which protects your National Insurance credits).

---

### **What Happens After the Extension Period?**

After the 20-week extension period ends (or when Alex turns 18), Child Benefit will stop **unless** Alex:
- Enrolls in approved full-time non-advanced education or training (then you can continue claiming until age 20)
- The education must be for at least 12 hours per week

I recommend applying promptly to make the most of this extension period. Good luck!
